fixes.row: Taken up into heaven (Elijah; Jesus ...); coming with the clouds of heaven or from heaven: “One like the Son of Man” ...
fixes.why: Dan 7:13 (Berean: “I saw One like the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven”) is a vision in the Aramaic of Daniel, and it is filed under a row whose label names Jesus (“the Lord Jesus”, “His Son”) and whose doors go to Jesus and to the Ascension. The label quotes the Daniel phrase as one of the New Testament names. Rule 5: an Old Testament verse is not filed under a New Testament heading as if it belonged there.
fixes.fix: Move Dan.7.13 out of this row into a row of its own, labelled from what the verse says (for example “One like a son of man, coming with the clouds of heaven to the Ancient of Days”), with no door to Jesus. In this row remove “One like the Son of Man” from the label and keep “the Son of Man”, “the Lord Jesus” and “His Son” for Matt 24:30, Matt 26:64, Mark 14:62, 2 Thess 1:7 and 1 Thess 1:10. The note's sentence on the same words in Matt 26:64 and Mark 14:62 stays, and it should name Dan 7:13 as the source. Row count goes to 27; the editor decides the count.

fixes.row: The Holy Spirit and heaven: descending from heaven, sent from heaven, given by the Father in heaven, lifting up between earth and heaven
fixes.why: Ezek 8:3 has “the Spirit” (rûaḥ) lifting Ezekiel up between earth and heaven, with no “Holy” in the Berean. Under a label that says “The Holy Spirit”, and with a door to the Holy Spirit card, a Hebrew prophet's spirit is filed as the New Testament person. Rule 5 and rule 1 (a label says only what its verses say).
fixes.fix: Remove Ezek.8.3 from this row. It already stands in row 14 (“In heaven and on earth: above and below, between heaven and earth”), so no verse is lost. Delete the clause in the note that says Ezek 8:3 “name[s] the Spirit in the verse as written”; keep the Luke 11:13 clause and the Heb 6:4 sentence.

fixes.row: Fallen or cast down from heaven to the earth: “day star”, stars, “the glory of Israel”, Satan; war in heaven with the dragon
fixes.why: Isa 14:12 (“O day star, son of the dawn!”) is said in the song of contempt “against the king of Babylon” (Isa 14:4, Berean). The verse does not name Satan. The label lists “Satan” among what falls and so reads the later Christian identification back into the Hebrew, which the note itself says readers part on. Rule 1 and rule 5.
fixes.fix: Relabel: “Fallen or cast down from heaven: “day star” (Isa 14:12, of the king of Babylon), stars, “the glory of Israel”; Satan (Luke 10:18); war in heaven with the dragon (Rev 12:7-8)”. Keep the note as it is; its sentence that readers part on whether these speak of one fall stays.

fixes.row: Jesus: “came down from heaven”, “the bread from heaven” (lead John.3.13, John.6.38, John.6.51, Rom.10.6)
fixes.why: Rom 10:6 in the Berean is “Who will ascend into heaven? (that is, to bring Christ down)”: the motion is going up, and the verse is Paul quoting Deut 30:12. The label is about coming down, and one of its four leads (Rom 10:6) shows the wrong motion. Any reader who opens the example sees the mismatch. The verse already stands in row 8 (looking up, ascending to heaven), where it fits.
fixes.fix: Remove Rom.10.6 from this row's pick and from its lead list. The lead then comes from the next fix (John.3.13, John.6.38, John.6.41, John.6.32). Rom.10.6 stays in row 8, where it already sits.

fixes.row: Jesus: “came down from heaven”, “the bread from heaven” (lead John.3.13, John.6.38, John.6.51, Rom.10.6)
fixes.why: The lead example, John 6:51 in the Berean, ends “this bread, which I will give for the life of the world, is My flesh”. Several Christian traditions read John 6:51-58 as speaking of the Lord's Supper (Catholic, Eastern Orthodox and some Lutheran readers) and others as speaking of believing in Christ (much of the Reformed and Baptist tradition). The row's label takes no side, but its lead puts the flesh-sentence first and its note says nothing; rule 2 asks that a divided passage be set beside a note that the page takes no side.
fixes.fix: Change the lead to John.3.13, John.6.38, John.6.41 and John.6.32 (all show “came down from heaven” with no flesh-sentence). Keep John.6.51 and John.6.58 in the row as written. Add to the note: “Readers part on whether John 6:51-58 speaks of the Lord's Supper or of believing in Christ; the page takes no side.”

fixes.row: Heavenly realms, things, bodies, calling, gift, country, Jerusalem, kingdom, host, vision (adjective form)
fixes.why: Matt 23:9 (Berean: “you have one Father, who is in heaven”) names the Father, and it sits in the heavenly-realms row, whose label names no Father and no person. Its word is the adjective οὐράνιος, so the adjective form is right and only the row is wrong.
fixes.fix: Move Matt.23.9 to the row “Your heavenly Father; My heavenly Father” and extend that label to “the one Father who is in heaven (Matt 23:9)”. This is a divine-persons row, so the move is the editor's per-record decision (rule 3); the panel's view is that it fits there.

fixes.row: Sun, moon and stars; the host of heaven; the Queen of Heaven
fixes.why: In the Berean the title “Queen of Heaven” occurs only in Jer 7:18 and Jer 44:17-25 (checked in data/bible/verses.bsb.jsonl), where it is the figure the people burn incense to. The label puts her in the list with the sun, moon and stars, which reads her as one more heavenly object. In the Catholic and Orthodox traditions the same title is a Marian one, so the juxtaposition, and the note's silence on the title's one use, could read as a comment on that devotion. The page makes no such comment, but the label should not do the work for a reader.
fixes.fix: Relabel to separate the title from the heavenly bodies: “Sun, moon and stars; the host of heaven; and the Queen of Heaven, to whom incense is burned (Jer 7:18; 44:17-25)”. Add to the note: “In the Berean the title occurs only in Jer 7:18 and Jer 44:17-25, and there the page does not name the figure.” Keep the rest of the note.

fixes.row: Not named in the verse: “He”, “the One”, “the second man”, “the Lord”, “a Master”, “Faithful and True” (door to Jesus)
fixes.why: The row's door sends every verse that names no one to the Jesus card. The note says readers take these verses of Jesus, of the Father, or otherwise, and that the page does not choose. The door chooses for them. Eph 6:9 and Col 4:1 (“a Master in heaven”) are the verses a conservative reader would most expect to see sent to the Father or left open, and the door does not leave them open.
fixes.fix: Remove the door to Jesus from this row (doors: none). The note already says the page does not choose; keep it as written. The verses stay where they are.

fixes.row: “Heaven” standing alone: “against heaven”, “from heaven or from men”, “Heaven rules”
fixes.why: The note says the text says “heaven” and the page does not say whom it stands for. The same chapter supplies the context: in Dan 4:25 (Berean) “the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind”, and 4:26 is the sentence that acknowledgement restores. A reader from the Hebrew Scriptures can see the chapter's own subject, and the note's silence about it makes the Aramaic look more open than the chapter is. Rule 1: nothing missing from what the text supplies.
fixes.fix: Keep the note's first sentence. Add: “The same chapter has “the Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind” (Dan 4:25) just before “Heaven rules” (Dan 4:26); the page sets the two side by side and does not say they name one and the same.”

fixes.row: A new heaven and a new earth; the holy city coming down out of heaven
fixes.why: The row leads with Isa 65:17 and the note's first clause is about the new heaven and earth, but the note names only New Testament verses (2 Pet 3:13; Rev 21:2, 21:10). The Hebrew Scriptures' own promise, Isa 66:22 (Berean: “the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make”), is not in the note. Rule 5: the Hebrew Scriptures heard on their own terms first.
fixes.fix: Open the note with the Isaiah verses: “I will create new heavens and a new earth” (Isa 65:17) and “the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make” (Isa 66:22), then the existing 2 Pet 3:13 and Rev 21:2, 21:10 sentence as it stands.

fixes.row: “others”: Other words translated “heaven”, “sky” (the Hebrew שַׁחַק, 12 verses): example 2 Sam 22:12
fixes.why: The block's title says these words are translated “heaven” or “sky”. Its second example, 2 Sam 22:12, reads in the Berean “a gathering of water and thick clouds”: the word is there, but the English does not show the label. Rule 6 (every example shows its label). The Hebrew strip gives “sky”, but a reader sees the Berean's English.
fixes.fix: Replace the example 2Sam.22.12 with Job.37.18, which is already in the word's verse list and whose Berean reads “can you, like Him, spread out the skies, as strong as a mirror of bronze?” (checked 2026-10-25).

worker_points.point: Rows 21, 22 and adjective row 26: heaven at death, or a new heaven and earth (each with a no-side note)
worker_points.why: No verse in the hub says “at death” with heaven in it; the three rows state what the verses say and their notes take no side. The Catholic and Orthodox seats may later want a door to the intermediate-state cards, but nothing shown misleads them.

worker_points.point: Row 4: renewed or replaced; “pass away” and “signs in heaven” in one row
worker_points.why: The label separates the two claims with a semicolon, the note names the Old Testament setting of most verses, and it takes no side. The signs are the verses' own wonders and demands for a sign.

worker_points.point: Row 18: verses with no name; whether the note's sentence is a lean
worker_points.why: The note's sentence (readers take them of Jesus, of the Father, or otherwise) describes readers and is fair. The lean is the door to Jesus on the same row; see the fix on that row.

worker_points.point: Rows 16, 17, 19: the persons by hand (Jesus' own I and My; Elijah and Jesus under one label; Dan 7:13 beside Matt 24:30; the Spirit)
worker_points.why: Dan 7:13 is filed under a New Testament heading (rabbi, rule 5); Ezek 8:3 under “The Holy Spirit” (rabbi); Rom 10:6 under “came down” (all seats, a misfit); John 6:51 leads row 16 with a flesh-sentence and no note (Reformed, Baptist).

worker_points.point: Row 20: fallen from heaven (Isa 14:12; Luke 10:18; Rev 12:7-8); whether one fall
worker_points.why: The label names Satan, and Isa 14:12 does not. The note already leaves open whether these are one fall, so the fix is the label only.

worker_points.point: Row 13: kingdom of heaven against kingdom of God (Matt 13:11; Mark 4:11; Luke 8:10); all 31 in Matthew
worker_points.why: The note says the page does not say the two are one. The door to the kingdom-of-God card is a link, not an equation, and the note covers it; the rabbi and the Baptist seat would see nothing said beyond the verses.

worker_points.point: Row 1: host of heaven in one row (the idols; the host beside the throne; Neh 9:6; the Queen of Heaven)
worker_points.why: One row for the host is fine: the note lists which verse is which. The Queen of Heaven sits in the label among the heavenly bodies, which is the fix (Catholic and Orthodox seats).

worker_points.point: Row 23: “Heaven” alone; whom it stands for
worker_points.why: The note's “does not say whom it stands for” leaves out what Dan 4:25 supplies in the same chapter (the Most High rules). The fix adds the context and keeps the page's silence about identity.

worker_points.point: Row 5: Acts 4:12 (no other name under heaven) in the row, not leading it
worker_points.why: The verse is under the label as written, and the lead is a neutral example. Baptist and Reformed readers would find the salvation verse neither promoted nor hidden.

worker_points.point: Rows 3, 9, 12 against the Trinity (Matt 11:25 and Luke 10:21 under “The LORD, God”; “Our Father in heaven” as Jesus' address)
worker_points.why: The rows are separate and no equation is made. Matt 11:25 and Luke 10:21 name the Father under the God row by hand; Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant readers would each take that as the text's own naming.

worker_points.point: Row 2: Rev 14:6, 8:13, 19:17 (“overhead”, “midair”) for the Greek mid-heaven
worker_points.why: The note says what the Greek word is and that the Berean prints “midair” or “overhead”; the sky row does not call the Greek heaven.

missing.what: Pentecost. The sound that “came from heaven” (Acts 2:2) is in row 6 (a sound from heaven), and the Spirit is named only in Acts 2:4, which has no heaven word, so the Spirit row cannot take it by rule. A Pentecostal reader expects the link. A note on the Spirit row pointing to Acts 2:2-4 (the sound from heaven, then the Spirit filling them) would show where the Spirit comes at Pentecost without changing any row.

examples_checked: 25 of 26 rows' examples show their label (row 16: Rom 10:6 does not); the “others” block: 2 Sam 22:12 does not. All 104 noun and adjective row examples were read against their labels, and the Berean was checked directly for the examples that carry a fix.
summary: The hub is largely true to the text and placed with care, with eleven fixes needed: the rabbi's objections are Dan 7:13 under a New Testament heading, Ezek 8:3 under “The Holy Spirit”, and the Satan label on Isa 14:12, and the Christian seats' objections are Rom 10:6 and Matt 23:9 mis-filed, the Queen of Heaven label, the John 6:51 lead, and a door that chooses for the unnamed verses. None of the fixes requires a doctrinal verdict, and each one moves a verse, a label or a note toward what its verses say.
